create.name: Ya'Acov Darling Khan
create.bio:
Ya'Acov Darling Khan is a British dance teacher and contemporary shaman who, with his wife Susannah, created Movement Medicine, a practice of conscious, ecstatic dance. The couple met in 1986 and began teaching in 1989 after training with Gabrielle Roth in her 5Rhythms work, studying with her for some eighteen years before shaping their own approach. In 2007 they founded the School of Movement Medicine, which now runs workshops, apprenticeships and professional trainings through teachers in many countries.

Movement Medicine blends free-form dance with ritual, ceremony and reflective enquiry, and asks dancers to treat what life has handed them as material for a more creative and responsible way of living. Ya'Acov's own path has also taken him into shamanic practice, and he has spent time with indigenous communities from the Arctic to the Ecuadorian Amazon, including the Sapara people, whose leader Manari Ushigua wrote the foreword to his first book. He has written two books of his own, Jaguar in the Body, Butterfly in the Heart and Shaman, and co-wrote Movement Medicine with Susannah. Today he teaches residential workshops in Europe, monthly lessons and seasonal online ceremonies through the school's Study Hub, and one-to-one sessions.

courses.title: Returning Home 2026 (Winter Solstice workshop, Kiental, Switzerland)
courses.description: A five-day residential dance workshop for the winter solstice with Ya'Acov and Susannah and two other teachers, using movement, art and ritual theatre to look back over the year and seed the next. Taught in English with German translation.

courses.title: Winter Solstice Tribal Heart (online ceremony)
courses.description: A two-and-a-half-hour online dance ceremony led by Ya'Acov and Susannah to mark the longest night, open to newcomers with a single ticket as well as Study Hub members.

courses.title: The Movement Medicine Study Hub
courses.description: The school's online membership: a monthly theme explored through a live movement class, short embodiment practices, sharing circles and recordings, plus the seasonal online ceremonies.
